channel.title: Acme: W3C Changes
channel.description: Reports on substantive changes in W3C GitHub repositories.

item.title: WCAG 2 Clarifies When Labels and Instructions Are Required
item.description:
WCAG’s understanding document for Labels or Instructions now distinguishes fields that need visible labels from controls whose purpose is already evident from surrounding context. It emphasizes that authors must provide enough information for users to know what input is expected, including formats and required values.

The revision also clarifies that the criterion does not require every control to carry a visible label when its purpose is otherwise unambiguous. The change is explanatory guidance, not a new WCAG requirement.

Changes: wcag commit 457cece2.

item.title: SHACL Node Expressions Gain Broader Examples and a Corrected hasLang Function
item.description:
The developing SHACL 1.2 Node Expressions draft has expanded its examples and synchronized code snippets across JSON-LD and Turtle. The examples now cover additional vocabularies and more realistic data-processing patterns.

A follow-up correction changes the SPARQL hasLang node-expression function to its proper one-argument form: it tests whether a term is a language-tagged literal rather than comparing against a second language argument.

Changes: data-shapes commit 91ec2bfa; data-shapes commit 71ecc01c.

item.title: CSS Defines Media Playback While content-visibility Is Hidden
item.description:
CSS Containment Level 2 now says that media inside content-visibility: hidden content keeps advancing rather than pausing, while its audio output is suppressed. Media state queries continue to reflect the live playback state, but queued media events wait until the content is no longer skipped.

The behavior extends into nested frames. Picture-in-picture output may remain audible, and content skipped only because of content-visibility: auto is explicitly unaffected so off-screen audio can continue playing.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 40527902.

item.title: MathML Polyfills Preserve Accessible Source Math
item.description:
W3C’s MathML polyfills now leave the original mathematical markup in the light DOM for assistive technology while hiding the generated visual shadow tree. The change lets tools such as MathCAT serialize and navigate the source expression instead of encountering only the transformed rendering.

The update also adds navigation-oriented tagging and clones carry content when building elementary-math layouts, preventing the rendering step from removing information from the accessible source.

Changes: mathml-polyfills commit cdc8850f; mathml-polyfills commit 67a557c6.

item.title: Draft Sustainability Guidelines Add Security Boundaries
item.description:
The draft Web Sustainability Guidelines now qualify longevity advice with security and operational constraints. Maintaining compatibility should not mean keeping unsafe components in service, and non-standard code should be retired when its risks outweigh its value.

The update adds a success criterion and propagates the revised guidance through the group’s quick reference, resources, impact data, and test pages.

Changes: sustainableweb-ig commit 6e27c1a0; sustainableweb-wsg commit eb8f8af2.

item.title: W3C’s Gargantua Tool Reports GitHub Failures More Reliably
item.description:
Gargantua’s GitHub client now recognizes the fetch layer’s actual error type and derives messages from the failed response correctly. Server failures and other API errors should therefore reach users as useful diagnostics instead of triggering secondary exceptions.

The update also moves its request trace identifier to shared scope so related telemetry can be correlated across calls.

Changes: gargantua commit 09aca318.

item.title: CSS Media Queries Adds an Application Display Mode
item.description:
Media Queries Level 5 now proposes an application value for the display-mode media feature. It identifies browsing contexts that are part of an installed or otherwise application-like experience.

Display modes are no longer modeled as mutually exclusive: an application running fullscreen can match both application and fullscreen. Child contexts inherit the top-level context’s matching modes.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 070e0210.

item.title: W3C Groups Server Warns About Retiring GitHub APIs
item.description:
The W3C groups service now watches GitHub API responses for Deprecation and Sunset headers. When GitHub marks an endpoint for retirement, the service emails an alert containing the request, API version, relevant dates, and migration links.

Duplicate notices are suppressed during a process lifetime, giving maintainers early warning without flooding them for every repeated request.

Changes: groups-server commit 2571abff.

item.title: MathML Polyfills Add maction and mstyle Support
item.description:
W3C’s MathML compatibility package now polyfills maction selection, toggling, and tooltips, with tests and integration into the combined build.

A separate addition brings MathML 3 mstyle defaults to MathML Core environments. It propagates inherited presentation attributes before other transforms run, helping older mathematical markup render consistently in current browsers.

Changes: mathml-polyfills commit b4fdca99; mathml-polyfills commit ae29d50d.

item.title: Draft Linked Web Storage Charter Adds Tentative Services
item.description:
The draft Linked Web Storage Working Group charter now lists tentative Recommendation-track deliverables for type indexing, type search, and notifications. Adoption depends on editor-draft maturity, interest from multiple implementers, and group consensus.

The draft also moves several expected completion dates and says interoperability must include independent implementations working with one another, not only passing open test suites.

Changes: lws-wg-charter commit 61b37b90; lws-wg-charter commit 3b96eb03; lws-wg-charter commit 7a997d06.

item.title: Updated French WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 Translations Become Authorized
item.description:
W3C’s accessibility site now points to updated authorized French translations of WCAG 2.1 and WCAG 2.2, both dated September 22, 2026.

The catalog replaces temporary candidate-translation entries and older records with the final W3C-hosted versions, giving French-speaking readers a stable authoritative reference.

Changes: wai-website commit 81b9b46e.

item.title: Linked Web Storage Limits Its Container Shape to Its Own Media Type
item.description:
The Linked Web Storage draft now requires the LWS container shape only for application/lws+json representations. Generic JSON-LD responses are no longer implicitly treated as the same restricted profile.

The repository also adds automated checks that tabbed serializations in examples describe isomorphic RDF, reducing the chance that JSON-LD, Turtle, and other forms drift apart.

Changes: lws-protocol commit ecce8a7d.

item.title: W3C Opens Namespace Requests to Community Groups
item.description:
W3C’s namespace guidance now defines how a Community Group can request a w3.org/ns URL. A chair must submit a proposed shortname and namespace document for review.

The document must identify the work as Community Group incubation and must not imply that it is a W3C standard. Requests can be rejected when they are confusing, offensive, or primarily commercial.

Changes: guide commit 2e2d1c00.

item.title: W3C Process Guidance Expands Review and Council Rules
item.description:
W3C’s operational guides now define “deciders” in Council proceedings, apply participant-suspension guidance to Councils and their chairs, and spell out the preparation expected before a TAG architecture review.

The wide-review guide also confirms that Registry-track publications need to demonstrate wide review just as Recommendation-track documents do unless the Process explicitly provides an exception.

Changes: guide commit 7c6972c7; guide commit d5a74ce2; guide commit fb3110fe; guide commit 00443a53.

item.title: W3C Group Feeds Now Support Task Forces
item.description:
W3C’s website frontend now accepts task-force identifiers in the group-feed route.

Task forces can therefore expose the same feed endpoint already available to Working Groups, Interest Groups, Community Groups, Business Groups, and other W3C functions.

Changes: w3c-website-frontend commit 869d42df.

item.title: Draft Note Examines Intentional Friction in Games
item.description:
A first substantive draft of a W3C Note examines cases where removing every obstacle can undermine a game or interface even though unnecessary friction creates accessibility barriers.

The draft distinguishes information discovery, presentation, and encoding, and outlines six possible responses. It explicitly still needs tone work, citations, decisions on some sections, and external review.

Changes: intentional-friction commit e4a73529.

item.title: Message Resources Draft Establishes a Portable Localization Format
item.description:
A new W3C draft defines a general-purpose container for localizable messages, including a data model, file serialization, metadata, sections, comments, and processing rules. It is designed especially for Unicode MessageFormat content without binding authors to one localization platform.

The syntax is now maintained as an external ABNF file imported by the specification, making the grammar independently testable and easier for implementations to consume.

Changes: message-resources commit 5f19cffa; message-resources commit 309e946c; message-resources commit 675cad06; message-resources commit 9336043d.

item.title: Reffy Improves Link Attribution and SVG Extraction
item.description:
Reffy now annotates both raw links and autolinks with the shortname of the specification they target, restoring source attribution after its link data was split into separate groups.

Its SVG 2 extraction rules also recognize SVG-specific property-definition tables and rely more directly on the specification’s improved Bikeshed markup. Together the changes make generated Web-platform reference data more complete.

Changes: reffy commit ab8c559b; reffy commit d8518856.

item.title: SHACL Clarifies Shape Rules and Global Rules
item.description:
The SHACL 1.2 Inference Rules draft now explains that a shape rule runs separately for each focus node, with SPARQL’s $this variable pre-bound, while a global rule runs without focus nodes.

Although shape-rule evaluation is local, its inferred triples are not: both kinds of rules add results to the same data graph. The clarification makes execution and data visibility more explicit for implementers.

Changes: data-shapes commit 1fd4d984.

item.title: CSS Mixins Reserve Cascade Layers for Future Design
item.description:
The CSS Mixins draft now makes @layer invalid inside a mixin body. When a mixin is applied, the contents of a nested @layer are dropped.

The restriction deliberately leaves room for a future level to define layer behavior without locking implementations into premature cascade semantics.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 16377320.

item.title: Long Animation Frames Exposes Source Locations and Rendering Durations
item.description:
The Long Animation Frames draft now exposes sourceLine and sourceColumn on PerformanceScriptTiming entries, giving performance tools a direct location for expensive script work.

It also separates styleDuration and layoutDuration on frame timing entries. Developers can distinguish time spent recalculating styles from time spent laying out the page instead of seeing only a combined phase.

Changes: long-animation-frames commit 0ad24fe9; long-animation-frames commit 14c0dc63.

item.title: CSS Adds Interest Indicators and Interest-State Selectors
item.description:
CSS Pseudo-Elements and Selectors drafts now define an interest button for elements that expose additional information through hover, focus, or explicit activation. Related selectors distinguish an interest source from its target.

The developing feature is designed to support HTML’s interestfor mechanism across mouse, keyboard, and touch environments, including controls that already perform another action when activated.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 247bc6b2; csswg-drafts commit 9f78c40e.

item.title: EPUB Annotations Adds Detailed Privacy Guidance
item.description:
The EPUB Annotations draft now explains how notes, highlights, bookmarks, selected passages, and reading histories can expose political, health, religious, or other sensitive information.

It calls for data minimization, explicit sharing controls, secure storage and transport, careful synchronization, and clear retention and deletion behavior in reading systems and annotation servers.

Changes: epub-specs commit 20c32131.

item.title: Internationalization Tests Add EPUB Reading-System Results
item.description:
W3C’s internationalization test suite now has a section for EPUB reading systems, which consume packaged publications rather than browser URLs.

The first test books cover vertical text-emphasis positioning and are scored manually against criteria embedded in each EPUB. Sources and build tooling are included alongside a results table.

Changes: i18n-tests commit 6ab56f2c.

item.title: Geolocation Sensor Is Marked Discontinued
item.description:
The Devices and Sensors Working Group roadmap now marks the Geolocation Sensor API as discontinued and links to the February 3, 2026 discontinuation publication.

The status makes clear that the draft is no longer progressing on the standards track.

Changes: das-wg commit d59eba8b.

item.title: WCAG2ICT Applies WCAG’s Level AAA Caveats Beyond the Web
item.description:
The WCAG2ICT draft now carries WCAG’s two Level AAA cautions into non-Web documents and software.

It explains that AAA criteria are being mapped for these contexts while retaining WCAG’s warning that requiring complete AAA conformance as a general policy is not appropriate for all content.

Changes: wcag2ict commit add4bd94.

item.title: CSS Line Clamping Excludes Suppressed Boxes from Baselines
item.description:
CSS Overflow Level 4 now says that visually suppressed boxes do not participate in the first or last baseline set of a line-clamp container.

The clarification prevents content hidden by clamping from shifting the baseline used to align the container with surrounding layout.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 26180f5e.

item.title: Input Events Lets Authors Initialize Target Ranges
item.description:
The Input Events draft now explicitly allows InputEventInit.targetRanges to initialize the ranges returned by getTargetRanges(). This gives synthetic editing events a defined way to identify the content they would modify.

New non-normative guidance also tells editors how to handle synthetic beforeinput events from spelling and grammar extensions, including replacement, paste, and deletion operations.

Changes: input-events commit e69ef15b; input-events commit b4875c8e.

item.title: CSS Aligns Corner Shorthand Serialization Order
item.description:
CSS Borders Level 4 now lists corner shape before border radius in the grammar for corner shorthands, matching the working group’s resolution.

The order affects canonical serialization while preserving the shorthand’s ability to accept the two components in either order.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 9defc4a4.

item.title: IFT Encoder Retunes Automatic Quality for Large Fonts
item.description:
The Incremental Font Transfer encoder has new automatic quality buckets derived from measured segmentation times across the Google Fonts collection. The thresholds target no more than roughly 0.5 percent of fonts in a bucket taking at least 15 minutes.

A new utility calculates candidate buckets from benchmark data, making future tuning reproducible instead of hand-maintained.

Changes: ift-encoder commit c8ac79e0; ift-encoder commit 662773ff.

item.title: CSS Explores Mesh and Freeform Two-Dimensional Gradients
item.description:
A new CSS Images Level 5 explainer proposes mesh-gradient() and freeform-gradient() for colors that vary across two dimensions rather than along a line or circle.

The proposal compares mesh patches with diffusion-style control points, discusses editing and PDF serialization, and remains exploratory rather than standardized syntax.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 47c467ed.

item.title: SPARQL Rules Draft Defines Grouping and Aggregation
item.description:
The developing SPARQL Rules language now defines aggregation elements, their well-formedness conditions, and execution order. Rules with aggregation run once after rules that may produce their input and before rules that depend on their output.

An aggregate is calculated over the complete collection of contributing triples. The draft also begins enumerating supported aggregation functions.

Changes: data-shapes commit c24a4158; data-shapes commit 72a0523d.

item.title: Linked Web Storage Adopts RFC 9728 Authorization Discovery
item.description:
Linked Web Storage now uses OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata for authorization-server discovery. A 401 response must provide RFC 9728’s resource_metadata parameter pointing to the requested resource’s metadata document.

The change replaces custom as_uri and realm challenge parameters with the standardized discovery mechanism and updates security guidance accordingly.

Changes: lws-protocol commit 9420b5d6.

item.title: WCAG2Mobile Narrows and Explains Its Scope
item.description:
The WCAG2Mobile draft now states more clearly that it interprets WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA for native, cross-platform, hybrid, and mobile Web applications.

It also warns that WCAG does not cover every mobile accessibility need and explains why Web concepts such as user agents and sets of pages require interpretation in app environments. The document remains informative.

Changes: matf commit 4a91ccb8.

item.title: Paint Timing Excludes Non-Paintable Iframes from First Paint
item.description:
The Paint Timing draft now counts an iframe’s enclosing box toward first paint only when the iframe is paintable.

This ties the metric to the same visibility and rendering conditions used elsewhere in the specification, avoiding first-paint signals from frames that cannot actually contribute visible content.

Changes: paint-timing commit 4bceb4c5.

item.title: SVG 2 Aligns Script Processing with HTML
item.description:
SVG 2 now defines its script element by reference to HTML’s script processing model. SVG scripts consequently share HTML’s type values, including module, and the type attribute no longer assumes a default media type.

The alignment reduces a long-standing behavioral difference between inline SVG documents and HTML.

Changes: svgwg commit 4f4a0d8e.

item.title: SVG Images and Scripts Gain Referrer Policy Controls
item.description:
SVG 2 now adds referrerpolicy and matching referrerPolicy IDL attributes to image and script elements, paralleling HTML’s img and script controls.

Authors can therefore control referrer information for externally loaded SVG images and scripts without relying on document-wide policy.

Changes: svgwg commit 192731cb.

item.title: SVG textPath Animation Follows Path Data Rules
item.description:
SVG 2 now states that textPath’s path attribute animates under the same structural interpolation rules as the d property.

Smooth interpolation requires compatible command structures; otherwise the animation uses discrete behavior. The clarification aligns text-on-path animation with ordinary path animation.

Changes: svgwg commit e4e67949.

item.title: Ask I18N Adds Bounded Response Caching
item.description:
The Ask I18N service now caches generated answers for 15 minutes, keyed by question, language, filters, model settings, and the loaded search index.

The cache holds at most 256 entries, removes expired responses, and shares an in-flight promise for identical concurrent requests. Reloading the index automatically creates a fresh cache.

Changes: ask-i18n commit bfe73506.

item.title: Attribution Reporting Requires Constant-Time Conversion Lookup
item.description:
The Attribution Reporting proposal now requires measureConversion() to return in time independent of the number of stored impressions or concurrent requests.

The constant-time requirement closes a timing side channel that could otherwise reveal information about saved attribution state. The API remains proposal work.

Changes: attribution commit 4ce6dbfe.

item.title: VC-ALM Test Suite Adds Required Endpoint Coverage
item.description:
The VC-ALM interoperability suite has added endpoint-driven tests for credential issuance, verification, holder and workflow behavior, and status updates.

It now includes OpenAPI validation, negative fixtures, reusable assertion helpers, and scheduled report generation, giving implementers broader automated coverage of required protocol endpoints.

Changes: vcalm-test-suite commit df62bbd0.

item.title: Secure Payment Confirmation Validates Locale Lists More Precisely
item.description:
The Secure Payment Confirmation draft now defines locale validation in terms of well-formed language tags and language subtags, with ASCII case-insensitive matching where appropriate.

The revised steps clarify how a caller’s ordered locale preferences are checked and selected for the payment confirmation experience.

Changes: secure-payment-confirmation commit 1877eaa1.

item.title: Verifiable Credential Render Methods Rename Templates to Payloads
item.description:
The Verifiable Credential Render Method draft has renamed the suite field template to payload. A payload may be an inline map, a data URL, or another URL whose content is used by the rendering suite.

The broader term avoids implying that every suite operates on a traditional template and updates conformance language across all suites.

Changes: vc-render-method commit ba7a583f.

item.title: WebCodecs Tightens AV1 Chunk Requirements
item.description:
The WebCodecs AV1 registration now defines an encoded chunk as one temporal unit of low-overhead OBUs, with an optional initial temporal delimiter.

A key chunk must carry a sequence header before its first frame header, and that frame must be a shown key frame rather than an existing-frame reference. The added constraints make random-access expectations precise.

Changes: webcodecs commit 97421577.

item.title: SVG Path Segment Lookup Uses Base Path Data
item.description:
The proposed getPathSegmentAtLength() API now operates on the base value of the d attribute, not computed or animated path data, and returns a segment from the unnormalized base sequence.

The draft also removes an unreachable NaN branch: Web IDL rejects NaN and infinity for the float argument before the algorithm runs.

Changes: svgwg commit 187b470e; svgwg commit 276cdb57.

item.title: DID Resolution Draft Reworks URL Dereferencing
item.description:
The DID Resolution draft has completed a broad revision of its isolated DID URL dereferencing algorithm. The new flow separates strategy selection from resource handling and documents the decision points with updated diagrams.

The work aims to make dereferencing behavior implementable across DID methods while keeping method-specific handling explicit.

Changes: did-resolution commit 0956c939.

item.title: CSS Parser Entry Points Return to Declaration Lists
item.description:
CSS Syntax Level 3 has removed the unused “parse a block’s contents” entry point and restored an explicit algorithm for parsing a list of declarations. That entry point is used for style attributes and CSSStyleDeclaration.cssText.

Related CSSOM text now serializes identifiers using the revised definition of non-ASCII identifier code points, keeping parsing and serialization aligned.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit fbd84ec6; csswg-drafts commit a8a0b410; csswg-drafts commit 87c9dbaa.

item.title: SOSA and SSN Publish Machine-Readable Ontology Mappings
item.description:
The SOSA and SSN draft now publishes its alignments to related ontologies in a spreadsheet using the Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings.

The tabular SSSOM form complements the prose specification and gives tools a machine-readable way to consume mapping versions and relationships.

Changes: sdw-sosa-ssn commit 610c0ae5.

item.title: AI Content Disclosure Community Report Reaches Final Status
item.description:
The W3C Community Group reports repository now contains the final October 9, 2026 report on AI content disclosure.

The report is Community Group work rather than a W3C Recommendation. Its publication records the group’s completed proposal for communicating AI involvement in content creation.

Changes: cg-reports commit 0e310e46.

item.title: Exploratory CSS Overscroll Level 2 Draft Adds Bound Areas
item.description:
An initial, explicitly exploratory CSS Overscroll Behavior Level 2 draft introduces overscroll containers and overscroll areas. Authors could bind an element to a scroll boundary and reveal or toggle it when overscrolling occurs.

The draft combines CSS properties with HTML command invokers, defines stacking and visibility behavior, and is an early design rather than a stable feature.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 2c470fff; csswg-drafts commit 01e9acb7; csswg-drafts commit 51e650f6; csswg-drafts commit cd75df4a; csswg-drafts commit aff76932.
